Electrician (General)

VPT Mechanical Solutions
Kalgoorlie-Boulder, WA 6430
Full-time | Permanent

Salary: $80,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation

About the Role

VPT Mechanical Solutions is seeking a qualified and experienced Electrician (General) to join our team in Kalgoorlie-Boulder, Western Australia. This full-time position is responsible for installing, testing, maintaining, repairing, and commissioning electrical equipment, wiring, and control systems while ensuring all work complies with relevant Australian standards and workplace safety requirements.

Key Responsibilities
Interpret electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, blueprints, and technical specifications to determine installation requirements and work sequences.
Measure, mark out, and prepare installation reference points for electrical systems and equipment.
Select, cut, terminate, and connect electrical wiring and cables to switches, outlets, control devices, and other electrical components.
Use electrical testing and diagnostic equipment to identify faults in electrical systems and circuits.
Repair and replace faulty wiring, electrical components, and other defective parts.
Install, connect, and commission electrical switchboards, distribution boards, and associated equipment.
Connect electrical systems and equipment to power supplies in accordance with applicable standards and regulations.
Test electrical circuits for continuity, insulation resistance, and operational performance to ensure safe and reliable operation.
Install, test, maintain, and commission solar photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems where required.
Complete electrical maintenance and modifications while ensuring compliance with workplace health and safety procedures and Australian electrical standards.
Skills, Qualifications and Experience

To be considered for this position, applicants must meet one of the following:

Hold an AQF Certificate III in Electrotechnology Electrician (or equivalent qualification); or
Have at least three (3) years of full-time relevant work experience as an Electrician (General).

The successful applicant will also demonstrate:

Current electrical licence or registration as required in Western Australia.
Sound knowledge of electrical systems, wiring methods, and Australian Standards.
Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings and technical documentation.
Proficiency in using electrical testing and diagnostic equipment.
Strong fault-finding and problem-solving skills.
High attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team.
Strong commitment to workplace health and safety.
A current driver's licence is desirable.

What We Offer

Full-time permanent employment.
Competitive annual salary of $80,000 – $85,000 plus superannuation.
Supportive and professional team environment.
Ongoing training and career development opportunities.
Long-term employment with an established and growing company.

About Us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory and beyond.

About the Employer
We are supporting an automotive business (ABN 69 669 060 913) based in Acacia Ridge, Queensland, specialising in Japanese vehicle imports, compliance, mechanical repairs, servicing, and vehicle inspections. With over 20 years of industry experience and a commitment to quality, safety, and customer satisfaction. The business is seeking a Motor Mechanic to support its growing operations and to maintain, test, diagnose and repair petrol engines and the mechanical components of lightweight motor vehicles, including transmissions, suspension, steering and braking systems.

Salary: $79,423 to $83,000 per annum plus superannuation
Location: Acacia Ridge, QLD
Employment Type: Full-time, ongoing
Ordinary Hours: 38 hours per week

Key Responsibilities
- Detect and diagnose mechanical and related electrical faults in petrol engines and vehicle components.
- Use automotive diagnostic scan tools, computers, multimeters, pressure gauges and other testing equipment to identify faults.
- Inspect and test petrol engines, transmissions, steering systems, suspension systems, brakes and related mechanical components.
- Dismantle and remove engine assemblies, transmissions, steering mechanisms and other mechanical components.
- Examine dismantled parts and components for wear, damage, defects and serviceability.
- Repair or replace worn, damaged and defective mechanical parts.
- Reassemble petrol engines and mechanical components following repairs.
- Test and adjust repaired mechanical components to confirm correct operation and performance.
- Perform scheduled maintenance services, including oil and filter changes, lubrication, fluid replacement and engine tune-ups.
- Diagnose and repair fuel, ignition, cooling and engine-management systems.
- Service and repair transmissions, steering, suspension and braking systems.
- Complete vehicle road tests and post-repair inspections.
- Confirm that repairs have been completed correctly and that vehicles operate safely.
- Follow manufacturer specifications, service manuals, technical bulletins and workshop procedures.
- Inspect vehicles for roadworthiness and identify repairs required to meet applicable roadworthiness standards.
- Issue roadworthiness or safety certificates where appropriately licensed or authorised.
- Respond to vehicle breakdown service calls where required.
- Accurately record diagnostic findings, repairs completed, parts used and further work recommended.
- Complete job cards, service records and workshop documentation.
- Safely operate vehicle hoists, mechanical tools, power tools and diagnostic equipment.
- Maintain a clean, safe and organised workshop.
- Comply with workplace health and safety and environmental requirements.
- Assist apprentices or junior workshop employees where reasonably required.

Selection Criteria
1. Light-vehicle mechanical expertise
Demonstrated experience maintaining and repairing petrol-powered passenger and light commercial vehicles.
2. Diagnostic skills
Ability to detect and diagnose mechanical and related electrical faults using automotive diagnostic equipment.
3. Mechanical repair skills
Experience repairing petrol engines, transmissions, brakes, steering and suspension systems.
4. Technical knowledge
Ability to understand and follow manufacturer specifications, service manuals and technical repair information.
5. Problem-solving ability
Ability to identify vehicle faults, determine suitable repair methods and resolve mechanical problems efficiently.
6. Quality workmanship
Strong attention to detail and commitment to completing repairs to an appropriate trade and safety standard.
7. Organisation
Ability to manage allocated workshop jobs, maintain accurate records and complete repairs within required timeframes.
8. Communication and teamwork
Ability to communicate repair findings clearly and work effectively with workshop staff, management and service personnel.
9. Safety awareness
Demonstrated understanding of workshop safety, safe equipment operation and environmentally responsible waste disposal.

Required Qualifications and Experience
- AQF Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology, AQF Certificate IV, or an equivalent recognised automotive mechanical qualification.
- Relevant practical experience servicing and repairing petrol-powered lightweight motor vehicles.
- At least three years of relevant experience
- Experience using automotive diagnostic scan tools and testing equipment.
- Experience diagnosing and repairing petrol engines and associated mechanical systems.
- Current driver licence.
- Ability to work full-time in Brisbane.

How to Apply
We are looking for a reliable, skilled, and safety-minded automotive professional to support vehicle servicing, repairs, inspections, and workshop operations while maintaining high standards of quality, efficiency, and customer service.

To apply, please submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter of no more than 300 words explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork. Please use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
- A written response of no more than 600 words describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role. Please structure your example or examples using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a professional and growing automotive business that values quality, safety, teamwork, reliability, and customer satisfaction, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Phone calls and walk-in applications will not be accepted.

Applications Close: 13 August 2026

A CHANCE TO WORK WITH THE BEST, TO BE THE BEST
BAPL is an Australian-owned and operated independent, specialist, business analysis consultancy. We help our customers to be successful with project initiatives by delivering exceptional business analysis, as a service. We love technology and we are great at making it work. We connect business with technology to improve business performance. We have extensive experience throughout Australia and abroad, providing business analysis as a service across the ASX 200, corporate, government and not-for-profit sectors.
Along with our consultancy services, BAPL also offers education services and a BA Centre of Excellence to our clients and our people. Our mantra is “delivery success” and our unique business model, and industry leading IP, enables us to do just that, which is to deliver successful outcomes consistently.

We require full time Business Analysis Consultants.

OUR VALUES
- Product and service value – we provide valuable products and services that meet agreed expectations and uplift client business analysis capability.
- Outcome-focused delivery – refining work practices to deliver outcomes efficiently, creating reusable assets for the Practice to leverage.
- Professionalism, practice & partnership – enriching our practice with a team of professionals who value and promote our cultural foundations of service excellence, professional development, family, fun, partnership, knowledge sharing, thought leadership, accountability, and resilience.
- Collaboration based on mutual respect – collaborating with customers and the Practice to achieve better outcomes, underpinned by mutual respect for the feelings, dignity, rights, and personal views of all. Retaining talented people through supportive, fair and respectful treatment, competitive remuneration, development opportunities and recognition.
- Community – Investing in the business analysis community, including our Practice, our customers and through our affiliations with peak industry associations, advocating for criticality of exceptional business analysis in improving business performance.

WHAT WE OFFER THE RIGHT CANDIDATE
- Opportunity to work at Australia's leading business analysis specialist practice.
- Exciting assignments across a wide range of industries and sectors, supporting Australia’s most innovative organisations to deliver high-profile projects.
- Contribute to the success of our customers by helping them become more successful with their software initiatives, products, and services.
- Develop deep knowledge of different domains applying BAPL IP.
- A supportive culture to help you become a leading business analysis specialist.
- Strong focus on career and professional/personal development including career planning, fortnightly development sessions, knowledge sharing sessions, training in the BABOK V3, access to a mentor, yearly in-house development days, and access to both the BAPL and IIBA development centres.
- Access to a network of highly skilled BA colleagues and management support at any time.
- Support in your business analysis certification.
- Engage in business analysis thought leadership through a variety of channels aimed at helping you build a strong personal brand including IP development, knowledge sharing, and driving the business analysis industry forward.
- Contribute to our positive culture with your diversity of experience, capabilities, and unique value.
- Career pathways into leadership positions as the organisation grows.

WHAT YOU NEED
- Essential Competencies, Skills, and Experience
- Minimum 1-2 years' experience delivering Business Analysis services.
- Experience delivering in Agile/traditional methodologies.
- Excellent stakeholder engagement and management skills across all capability levels.
- Experience facilitating workshops with a range of stakeholders.
- Experience in requirements elicitation, definition, traceability, and management across different delivery methodologies.
- Strong communication skills - both verbally and in written form - at all levels within an organisation (business and technical).
- Experience in business process analysis, process improvement and process modelling.
- Experience delivering BA services via web collaboration tools.

NOTE: All successful applicants will be subject to a Criminal History Check, in alignment with our customers' requirements.
If you meet all the essential criteria, please submit your CV via this Ad, citing all relevant experience in support of the criteria outlined above.

Salary offered is $75k to $85k

Rix Asset Maintenance is seeking experienced Site Supervisors to join our team in NSW, supporting a number of slope stabilization projects across the civil, mining and infrastructure sectors throughout New South Wales.

Full time positions available with projects located across New South Wales.

About the Role

As the Site Supervisor, you will oversee all aspects of geotechnical stabilization works including various Drilling operations, Anchor installation, Grouting, Anchor testing, Rock fall netting and catch fence installation, Steel fixing, Formwork, Concrete, Shotcrete, and Scaling.

This role requires a strong leader who can lead and manage rope access construction teams while ensuring safety, productivity, and quality standards are consistently met.

Key Responsibilities

* Supervision and coordination of rope access crews including subcontractors, suppliers, plant and equipment
* Ensure that plant, equipment, staff and subcontractors operate within safe working conditions and ensure that all operations meet the environmental, safety and legislative requirements
* Conduct pre-starts, toolbox talks, and safety briefings
* Complete daily reports, safety documentation, and permit systems
* Conduct risk assessments, pre-work safety checks and equipment inspections while ensuring compliance is within industry standards
* Oversee installation of ground support systems including rock bolts, mesh, and shotcrete preparation
* Monitor work quality and productivity of rope access teams

Required Qualifications & Experience

* IRATA Rope Access Certification (preferred)
* White card
* Driving licence
* Minimum 3 years experience in ground engineering / civil infrastructure
* Demonstrated experience supervising rope access teams
* Experience in slope stabilization, scaling, rock bolting, or geotechnical works
* Previous mining site experience strongly preferred
* Strong knowledge of rope access safety procedures and risk management

Key Attributes

* Strong leadership and communication skills
* Safety-focused mindset
